title: Origins: Palliant
description:
For some, an ill omen. 
For others, the last hope.
body:
Description copied from its entry in the Origins Discord server, seen [here](https://discord.com/channels/734127708488859831/1266280210421121045).

***Created for the Magic Market Jam***

*Rage, rage against the dying of the light...*

**Impact: 2**

**Soul Shepherd:** 
- When non-undead creatures that you haven't harmed die near you, they leave behind Echoes of themselves.
 - Echoes are immune to most damage and vanish after 30 seconds without intervention.
- Right-clicking an Echo with an empty hand will cause it to vanish and grant a Soul Shard.
 - You can consume Soul Shards by right-clicking with one in hand.

> **Spirit Essence:**
> Using a Soul Shard on an Echo will extend its remaining life.


**Fury of The Damned:**
- After consuming a Soul Shard, your next few attacks deal additional Magic damage.
 - This damage is increased against Undead enemies.

> **Mercy in Death:** 
> Killing a creature with a deadly status effect will grant a Soul Shard


**Delay the Inevitable:**
- Consuming a Soul Shard will grant temporary health and briefly protect you from lethal damage.
 - You can share Soul Shards with others by sneaking before using them.

> **Life Transference:**
> Sneaking while using a shard of Prismarine, Quartz, or Glass (any vanilla pane) allows you to sacrifice a quarter of your health to create a Soul Shard.


**Hollow Resonance:**
- Whenever an Echo vanishes near you, you gain Grief. While grieving, you experience 15% fatigue.
 - Fatigue reduces movement speed, break speed, and attack speed.
- If the vanished Echo is one of your tamed creatures, you gain additional effects based on how it vanished.
 - Effects are listed in the Origin menu as tooltips.

> **Overwhelmed:**
> Filling your Grief meter causes you to take damage.


**Soulnumbed:** 
- You gain 15% passive damage resistance.
- You receive 30% less healing.
- You regenerate significantly slower but no longer need full hunger to regenerate.



To add, simply navigate to your world's "datapack" folder and slap this bad boy in there.
